overview: Beach Energy is an ASX-listed independent oil and gas exploration and production company headquartered in Adelaide, South Australia, founded in 1961. The company produces gas, oil and natural gas liquids from operated and non-operated interests across five basins in Australia and New Zealand (Cooper Basin, Otway Basin, Perth Basin, Bass Basin and Taranaki Basin), with a strategic focus on the core hubs of East Coast Australia (Cooper and Otway Basins) and West Coast Australia (Perth Basin/Waitsia). Beach sells almost exclusively into the domestic Australian and New Zealand gas and oil markets, plus LNG cargoes swapped through the North West Shelf export facility.

business_model.summary: Beach is a commodity price-taker E&P that generates revenue from selling gas (via long-term Gas Sales Agreements and emerging market-linked/spot pricing), oil, LPG and condensate produced from operated and non-operated joint ventures. Revenue is transactional/production-based rather than recurring, driven by produced volumes and realized commodity prices (oil, domestic gas, and LNG-linked pricing). FY26 sales revenue was $1,801 million on production of 19.4 MMboe, down 10% YoY on lower liquids/gas volumes (Cooper Basin flood impacts, Otway field decline) partly offset by a 7% rise in realized gas price to $11.5/GJ and an additional LNG cargo. Customers are wholesale/industrial gas users, utilities, gas retailers and one LNG offtaker (BP, under an existing LNG Sale and Purchase Agreement) — a B2B/wholesale model, not direct-to-consumer.
business_model.customer_type: B2B/wholesale — industrial and utility gas customers, gas retailers, and LNG offtake to BP via swap arrangements at the North West Shelf
business_model.geographic_mix: East Coast Australia (Cooper Basin JV + Otway Basin) ~61% of FY26 production; West Coast Australia (Perth Basin/Waitsia) ~17%; Bass Basin (Tasmania) ~8%; New Zealand (Taranaki) ~7%; Western Flank (Cooper Basin oil) ~8%. Beach supplied approximately 19% of East Coast domestic gas demand in FY26.

competitive_position.market_position: Mid-cap independent E&P and one of the larger suppliers to the Australian East Coast domestic gas market (~19% of East Coast demand); a smaller, more diversified player on the West Coast following Waitsia startup. Not a scale leader like Santos or Woodside, but holds strategically important legacy infrastructure (Moomba Gas Plant interests, Otway Gas Plant, Port Bonython) that is difficult to replicate.

moat_factors.description: Beach operates key gas plants (Otway Gas Plant 205 TJ/day, Beharra Springs, Middleton) and holds interests in shared infrastructure (Moomba Gas Plant, Port Bonython export facility), giving cost and connectivity advantages over new entrants who would need to build processing capacity from scratch.

Decades of subsurface knowledge and existing well/pipeline infrastructure in the Cooper Basin (Western Flank, JV interests) lowers incremental development costs versus greenfield entrants; newly awarded ~7,000 km2 of adjacent Queensland exploration blocks extends this advantage.

100% of Beach's East Coast gas is sold domestically (no LNG export exposure on that coast), which could become a structural advantage — or takeover attraction — if the proposed Domestic Gas Reservation Scheme forces LNG exporters to redirect volumes to the local market.
Gas and oil are fungible commodities; Beach has no pricing power over commodity benchmarks and competes primarily on cost of supply and contract terms.

weaknesses: No pricing power — a price-taker on both oil (global benchmark-linked) and much of its domestic gas (contracted, subject to periodic price reviews)
Declining reserve base: 2P reserves have fallen from 283 MMboe (FY22) to 156 MMboe (FY26), roughly halving in four years, driven by production depletion outpacing additions
Significant non-operated exposure (Cooper Basin JV via Santos, Waitsia via Mitsui) limits Beach's control over operating costs, timing and capital decisions on ~47% of FY26 production
Small scale relative to Santos/Woodside limits access to the lowest-cost capital and bargaining power in domestic gas contract negotiations
History of major project cost/schedule overruns (Waitsia Stage 2 ran ~70% over original budget with repeated delays)

growth_drivers: Waitsia Gas Plant ramp-up to steady-state 250 TJ/day nameplate capacity (reached April 2026, still resolving early-phase commissioning issues) — expected to be a much larger earnings contributor in FY27 and beyond as a full year of production flows through

Otway Basin nearshore exploration (Enterprise East and Selie prospects in Flaxman/Waarre sandstones) targeting a final investment decision in H1 FY27, using existing Beach-operated infrastructure for low incremental capital cost
Moomba Central Optimisation project (Cooper Basin JV, FID reached FY26) expected to debottleneck upstream infrastructure, unlock production growth and extend asset life

New exploration acreage secured in FY26: ~7,000 km2 in the Cooper Basin (Queensland), Taroom Trough (ATP 2081, with Omega Oil and Gas and Tri-Star Group) and Otway Basin, providing running room for organic reserve replacement

West Coast structural gas deficit narrative: WA potentially facing supply shortfalls of up to 70 PJ/year in the early 2030s as coal retires, positioning Waitsia/Beharra Springs for continued high-margin domestic offtake

Capital redeployment from the ~$130 million implied-value VIC/L35 divestment (completed/pending FY27), freeing over $500 million of capital previously earmarked for the Artisan development toward higher-return growth options

Moomba CCS project — among the lowest-cost CCS developments globally, injected ~1.3 MtCO2e in FY26 (+25% YoY), supporting the equity emissions intensity reduction target (35% reduction by 2030) and potential future carbon-related revenue/optionality
Management explicitly flagged appetite for value-accretive M&A in FY27, funded by a strengthened balance sheet (10.6% net gearing, well below the <15% target)

business.description: 2P reserves fell from 283 MMboe in FY22 to 156 MMboe in FY26 — nearly halved in four years — despite some positive revisions from Western Flank drilling; sustained organic and/or M&A-driven reserve replacement is required to avoid a structurally shrinking production base.

Beach's largest growth project ran ~70% over budget and years behind schedule; even after reaching nameplate 250 TJ/day in April 2026, the plant experienced a Cyclone Narelle-driven shutdown and ongoing early-phase commissioning issues, meaning steady-state reliability is not yet proven.

business.risk: Natural field decline across mature assets
business.description: Otway Basin production fell 14% YoY and Taranaki Basin also declined on natural decline; without continued drilling and backfill investment, legacy assets will keep eroding production.

Cooper Basin JV (operated by Santos) and Waitsia (operated by Mitsui) together represent roughly half of production; Beach cannot unilaterally control costs, pace of development or operational decisions on these assets, as illustrated by 2025-26 flood impacts to Santos-operated Cooper Basin infrastructure.

Major Cooper Basin flooding in 2025 and again in early 2026, plus Cyclone Narelle affecting the North West Shelf/Waitsia, drove double-digit production declines at Western Flank (-35%) and disrupted the Waitsia ramp-up.

financial.description: Revenue and margins are directly exposed to oil price benchmarks and domestic/LNG-linked gas pricing, both subject to global supply-demand and geopolitical volatility; underlying NPAT fell 21% YoY in FY26 partly on weaker realized pricing dynamics.

As an operator of multiple mature production licences (Otway, Western Flank, Bass Basin, Cooper Basin interests), Beach carries growing restoration and decommissioning provisions that will need to be funded from future cash flow, particularly as assets approach end-of-life.

financial.risk: Capital intensity and funding of growth
financial.description: FY27 capex guidance of $600-700 million (up to 65% growth-related) requires continued strong operating cash flow; net debt already increased from a net cash position in FY22 to $387 million net debt in FY26.

regulatory.description: The proposed scheme would require LNG exporters to supply volumes equivalent to 20% of export volumes to the domestic market; Beach's management argues the design (as currently proposed) could distort price signals and discourage new investment even though Beach itself is a net domestic supplier — final design remains uncertain and could reshape East Coast market economics.

regulatory.risk: East Coast gas price review outcomes
regulatory.description: The Otway Basin offshore Gas Sales Agreement price review for the three years from 1 July 2026 was ongoing at FY26 year-end, with backdated pricing outcomes creating uncertainty for near-term realized prices.

Beach has equity emissions intensity reduction targets (35% by 2030) that require continued investment in initiatives like Moomba CCS; tightening carbon policy could raise compliance costs or constrain new development approvals.

macro.description: Geopolitical uncertainty is explicitly flagged by management as a driver of heightened price volatility affecting Beach's liquids revenue.

macro.risk: Australian east/west coast gas market structural imbalance
macro.description: While a potential tailwind for pricing, ongoing regulatory uncertainty around new gas supply investment (cited repeatedly by the Chair) creates a headwind to the timely development of new domestic supply that Beach itself depends on for growth.

Reporting is in AUD but oil and LNG-linked gas pricing references USD benchmarks, creating some currency translation exposure on realized pricing, though this is a secondary factor versus underlying commodity price risk.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian East Coast gas market: regulatory uncertainty (Domestic Gas Reservation Scheme) is constraining new supply investment even as new demand (including data centres) is expected to grow; the market is not currently seen as being in structural annual shortage, but southern-state seasonal deliverability is tightening. West Coast (WA) gas market: potential annual supply deficits of up to 70 PJ in the early 2030s as coal-fired generation retires and new industries (including data centres) emerge, a structural tailwind for Waitsia and Beharra Springs. New Zealand gas: major fields in structural decline with no material new developments, constraining Beach's Taranaki asset outlook. Global LNG/oil: near-term oil demand still growing but subject to heightened geopolitical volatility; LNG demand expected to grow as coal-to-gas switching accelerates.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — E&P earnings are directly leveraged to oil and gas prices and production volumes, both of which are cyclical and subject to weather/operational disruption (as seen with FY25-26 Cooper Basin flooding cutting production ~2% and driving the 21% NPAT decline).
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — capital-intensive project financing (Waitsia, Moomba Central Optimisation, exploration campaigns) and net debt of $387 million make Beach sensitive to funding costs, though net gearing of 10.6% (well below the <15% target) currently limits this risk.
key_input_costs: Steel/tubulars and gas plant construction/EPC costs (relevant to Waitsia-style projects)
Labour and contractor costs in a tight East/West Coast energy labour market

recent_developments.event: FY26 full-year results released: sales revenue $1,801m (-10% YoY), underlying EBITDA $1,040m (-8%), underlying NPAT $355m (-21%), statutory NPAT returned to profit at $281.4m (vs a prior-year statutory loss), full-year dividend cut to 3.0 cents per share fully franked (from 9.0 cps in FY25) as capital is redirected to growth.

FY27 guidance issued: production of 19.5-23.0 MMboe (up from FY26's 19.4 MMboe, reflecting a full year of Waitsia contribution) and capex of $600-700 million, with up to 65% directed to growth projects.

Beach agreed to sell its 60% operated interest in Otway permit VIC/L35 (containing the Artisan gas discovery) to Amplitude Energy (50%) and O.G. Otway (10%) for $70 million cash plus a production royalty of $3.75/GJ on up to 62 PJ through June 2036, implying total transaction value of ~$130 million and freeing over $500 million of previously committed development capital.

CEO Brett Woods publicly noted Beach's fully domestic-supply East Coast portfolio could make it an attractive acquisition target for LNG exporters if the proposed Domestic Gas Reservation Scheme is implemented, given LNG exporters would need to source additional domestic-market-committed volumes.

Waitsia Gas Plant reached nameplate capacity of 250 TJ/day, though a subsequent forced shutdown from Cyclone Narelle and ongoing early-phase commissioning issues moderated actual throughput through H2 FY26.

Waitsia Gas Plant achieved first sales gas, becoming Beach's most significant growth project delivered to date after a construction period marked by roughly 70% cost overruns and multi-year schedule delays.
Waitsia Gas Plant reached 'Ready for Start-Up' construction milestone.

Beach publicly opposing the government's proposed Domestic Gas Reservation Scheme (requiring LNG exporters to supply volumes equal to 20% of export volumes to the domestic market), arguing the current design adds no new supply and weakens investment price signals; final scheme design remained unresolved as of the FY26 results.
Shaun Gregory appointed to the Board as an independent non-executive director (elected November 2025).

Kerry Stokes-linked entities (Seven Group Holdings/Australian Capital Equity, via Chairman Ryan Stokes) continued to hold approximately 30% of Beach Energy, remaining the company's dominant shareholder bloc.

items.notes: Up from FY26 actual of 19.4 MMboe, driven primarily by a full year of Waitsia Gas Plant production as it moves toward steady-state operations.

Up to 65% allocated to growth projects (Western Flank exploration/appraisal, Otway nearshore FID, Cooper Basin JV drilling, Taroom Trough); sustaining capital expected below $450 million; abandonment expenditure to decrease post-Equinox rig campaign.

FY26 actual net gearing of 10.6% remains comfortably below the target; Capital Management Framework amended in FY26 to prioritise balance sheet strength ahead of shareholder returns while growth capital is deployed.
Supported by the Moomba CCS project, which injected ~1.3 MtCO2e in FY26 (+25% YoY) and is described as among the lowest-cost CCS developments globally.
Two-well campaign targeting the offshore Enterprise East and Selie prospects, using existing Beach-operated infrastructure.

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Ryan Stokes described FY26 as 'a year of consolidation' and said Beach enters FY27 'stronger, clearer in its strategy and repositioned for future growth,' while flagging the Board's intent to 'grow returns to shareholders' as the balance sheet strengthens, alongside pursuit of 'disciplined organic investment and value-accretive acquisitions.' CEO Brett Woods said Beach enters FY27 'in a resilient position' focused on 'building the resource base through targeted drilling and development programs' including an eight-well Western Flank exploration campaign, while cautioning that Waitsia was 'progressively resolving early-phase issues' toward steady-state operations and that regulatory uncertainty (the Domestic Gas Reservation Scheme) 'continues to weigh on market confidence' and could shape Beach's future investment decisions.

bull_case: Waitsia Gas Plant is now online and at nameplate capacity (250 TJ/day) after years of delay — FY27 will be the first full year capturing its earnings contribution, directly driving the raised FY27 production guidance of 19.5-23.0 MMboe

Strong balance sheet (10.6% net gearing, $983 million liquidity) provides flexibility to fund growth organically and pursue value-accretive M&A, with management explicitly signalling appetite for acquisitions

Structural West Coast gas deficit (potential shortfall of up to 70 PJ/year in the early 2030s) and East Coast domestic-only supply position Beach favourably versus LNG-export-exposed peers, and could even make Beach a take-out target for exporters needing domestic-committed volumes under a Gas Reservation Scheme

Portfolio optimisation (VIC/L35 sale freeing >$500 million of capital, redeployment toward higher-return Waitsia/Cooper Basin/Otway nearshore opportunities) demonstrates disciplined capital allocation under CEO Brett Woods since the FY24 strategic reset
Record safety performance (zero recordable injuries for a full financial year, first time in 15+ years) and >94% plant reliability at operated sites reflect improving operational execution culture
bear_case: 2P reserves have nearly halved in four years (283 MMboe FY22 to 156 MMboe FY26), raising questions about the sustainability of production beyond the medium term absent successful exploration or M&A

Waitsia's ramp-up remains unproven at steady-state — the project already ran ~70% over budget with multi-year delays, and even after reaching nameplate capacity in April 2026 it suffered a cyclone-driven shutdown and ongoing commissioning issues
FY26 dividend was cut two-thirds (from 9.0 cps to 3.0 cps) as capital is redirected to growth, and underlying NPAT fell 21% YoY — income-focused investors face reduced near-term cash returns

Unresolved Domestic Gas Reservation Scheme design creates meaningful regulatory overhang for the entire East Coast gas sector, with management warning a poorly designed scheme could weaken investment incentives industry-wide

Heavy exposure to weather-related disruption (repeated Cooper Basin flooding in 2025 and 2026, Cyclone Narelle impacting Waitsia) and natural field decline (Otway -14%, Western Flank -35%, Taranaki -17% in FY26) show operational fragility even before considering commodity price risk

Analyst sentiment is mixed-to-cautious — consensus rating is roughly 'Neutral/Hold' with a wide range of price targets, reflecting uncertainty about both near-term execution and the regulatory backdrop
